queue.title: The build-or-don't decision
queue.description: Most founders don't decide not to build — they just keep researching. The three things the decision actually needs, and why "ship something small and see" answers a different question.
queue.linkedinTeaser:
Founders: if you're "still researching" an idea you've already decided to build, you're not researching. You're delaying.

The build-or-don't decision needs three things: who pays (a person, not "the market"), what they'd stop doing to pay you instead, and the number that would make you walk away — decided before you're months and savings deep.

"Just ship something small and see" answers a different question — what to build, not whether to. If you'd have built it regardless of the answer, the market didn't decide. You did, before you started.

What's the number that would make you walk away from what you're building right now — and did you decide it before you started, or are you still deciding it?
